message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate this submission against the rubric.

C1 Introduction: mission concept, rationale, number of spacecraft, users. All addressed well with references. Accomplished: 8-9. The introduction is detailed, references literature [1]-[6]. Primary mission, why needed, one spacecraft with justification, users (operator AIMS, customers). Mark 9.

C2 Mission design: launch site/vehicle with justification, orbit type/elements, manoeuvres, ground control, comms frequency, mission duration, EOL. STK screenshots (Images 1-5), access tables, hand calculations (J2, launch azimuth, decay). Very comprehensive. Some minor issues: eclipse duration claim ~34 min at 600 km SSO — eclipse duration for 600 km circular is about 35 min max, fine. Drag calculation: Δa = 2π(C_D A/m)ρa² — check: da per orbit = 2π C_D (A/m) ρ a². With ρ=1e-13, a=6.978e6 m, A/m=0.3/50=0.006, C_D=2.2: Δa = 2π×2.2×0.006×1e-13×(6.978e6)² = 2π×2.2×0.006×1e-13×4.87e13 = 2π×2.2×0.006×4.87 = 2π×0.0643 = 0.404 m. Correct. Decay rate 0.40 m/orbit × 14.9 orbits/day × 365 = 2.2 km/yr. Correct. With sail: A/m = 4.3/50 = 0.086, Δa = 0.404×(0.086/0.006)=5.8 m. Correct. Lifetime ≈ H/rate: 70 km / 2.2 km/yr = 32 yr; 70/31 = 2.26 yr. Correct.

Sun-sync inclination: cos i = -0.1355 → i = 97.79°. Check: standard value at 600 km is ~97.79°. Correct.

Launch azimuth: sin β = cos i / cos φ = cos 97.79°/cos 5.2° = -0.1355/0.9959 = -0.136, β = -7.8°. Correct.

Ground track spacing: 2π×6378×5801/86164 = 2π×6378×0.06733 = 2698 km. Correct.

Data budget: 60,000 km² × 40,000 pixels/km² (5m GSD → 40,000 pixels per km²? 1 km² / (5m×5m) = 1e6/25 = 40,000. Yes) × 4 bands × 12 bits = 60,000×40,000×48 bits = 1.152e11 bits = 115 Gbit. Correct.

Access table: 6 passes/day, mean 580.8 s. Plausible for Hobart at 42.8°S with 97.79° inclination. Fine.

Minor issues: "latitude is lower than 180° minus the inclination" — should be inclination minus... actually for direct launch, latitude must be ≤ 180° − i for retrograde? For i=97.79, 180−i = 82.21°, and latitude 5.2° < 82.21°. That's correct actually: launch latitude must satisfy |φ| ≤ 180° − i for retrograde orbits. Fine.

Eclipse 34 min: at 600 km, orbital period 96.7 min, eclipse fraction... eclipse duration ~35.4 min max. 34 min plausible.

RAAN 27.33° with descending node crossing at 08:45 LMST — plausible.

Accomplished level: 9. Maybe 9. The design is comprehensive, accurate, persuasive, with STK screenshots, files, hand calcs, references. Mark 9.

C3 Conclusion: detailed, specific, includes limitations and future work. Accomplished: 8-9. Mark 8 or 9. It's quite detailed and specific. 9.

C4 Presentation: clear structure, executive summary, labelled figures/tables, references cited in text matching list. Check citations: [1]-[15] all cited in text? [1] yes, [2] yes, [3] yes, [4] yes, [5] yes, [6] yes, [7] yes, [8] yes, [9] yes, [10] yes, [11] yes, [12] yes, [13] yes, [14] yes, [15] yes. All cited. Writing quality high. Minor: some references vague ("Nature, news article", "The Space Review, article 3887" — incomplete titles). Mark 8.

Requirements: R1 yes, R2 yes, R3 yes, R4 yes, R5 yes, R6 yes, R7 yes, R8 yes, R9 yes (STK), R10 yes (screenshots + files listed in Appendix A), R11 yes.

Technical issues: minor — link budget not done (acknowledged); Mount Pleasant assumption of adding transmitters; Vega C not flown (acknowledged); reference [4] and [15] incomplete. Also "eclipse of about 34 minutes" — fine. The claim "sees six passes a day" — access table shows 6/day, fine.

Overall: strong submission, ~9/9/9/8 weighted: 0.1×9 + 0.6×9 + 0.1×9 + 0.2×8 = 0.9+5.4+0.9+1.6 = 8.8/10.
